Page.SourceString:
二十年前，一个叫伊南娜的名流邀请我的组织去一处秘密沙龙。她许诺凡参加者会获得丰厚的报酬。

也不知道算是幸运还是不幸，因为贪杯睡过头，我赶到时已经迟了，吃了闭门羹。当时我也不以为意，只是错过一桩生意罢了。但从那天起，我的同伴——赞恩、俄里翁、阿椿、蕾妮塔、里欧——他们就像人间蒸发了一样，再也没有出现过。我四处打听，那位名流也不知去向。
对了，说是组织——其实更像一个乱糟糟的家。我们这些人，要么是孤儿，要么是弃儿。这个世界除了我，不会有人在意他们的死活。所以找到他们理所应当地成为了我的重任。

这一找就是二十年。前不久，我在黑市上打听到伊南娜的消息。顺着线索找到她出奇地顺利，顺利得像是她一直在等我。见面后，她开门见山地告诉我，新的宴会即将开始，如果我参加，就能在席间的游戏里和同伴重逢——他们会在每一轮游戏中「重生」。

我恨伊南娜，但又希望她说的都是真的。我问她，如果我参加，能带他们离开吗？她笑了，说只要我能在游戏中胜出，就可以。

于是，我参加了雾巢游戏。
Page.LocalizedString:
Twenty years ago, a socialite named Inanna invited my organization to a speakeasy. She promised generous pay to anyone who attended.

Whether it was a coincidence, I still can't say. I drank too much and slept in, so by the time I got there, I was too late and got turned away at the door. At the time, I didn't think much of it. I figured I'd only missed out on a job. But from that day on, my companions—Zane, Orion, Tsubaki, Renita, and Rio—vanished off the face of the earth and were never seen again. I asked around everywhere, but the socialite had disappeared too.
I called it an organization, but it was really more like one big, messy family. We were all either orphans or abandoned children. In this world, no one but me would have cared whether those children lived or died. So, finding them became my responsibility.

I searched for twenty years. Recently, though, I got word of Inanna being seen in the Black Market. Following her trail was easy—as if she'd been waiting for me all along. When we met, she got straight to the point. A new banquet was about to begin, and if I joined it, I could reunite with my companions through "the game" there—they would be "reborn" every round.

I hate Inanna, and yet I wanted every word she said to be true. I asked her that, if I took part, could I bring them home? She smiled and replied that if I could win the game, I could take them away.

So, I entered the Fogden Game.

Page.SourceString:
宴会只是掩人耳目的幌子，真正的「游戏」简直残酷至极。进来雾巢我就后悔了，只能四处搜寻伊南娜的身影，誓要用她的鲜血祭奠我的同伴——直到来到了一处山谷之中。在这里，我看到了同伴留下的标记：「眼睛」。那图案是最小的同伴里欧之前随手画的，队长赞恩拿它来作为组织的标志。里欧的本领是绝对的方向感，不管在哪都不会迷路。

我顺着记号往深处走，看到了一条巨大的蛇怪。还没等我反应过来，它便哀鸣着往洞穴深处退去。沿途我看到其他人的残骸——它会攻击别人，却始终没有攻击我。

我一路追到山谷尽头，把它逼至绝境。它终于第一次回头面对我。大蛇的脑袋上，是蕾妮塔的脸。它的嘴和鸣叫声，像兽化后的俄里翁。那些蝴蝶般的鳞翅，和阿椿耳畔的一模一样。蛇身的构造，像赞恩的武器。还有那些布满全身的眼睛图案……里昂，是你涂的么？可惜你再也没能找到回家的路……

我会试着和它说话。如果它还有人的意识，还能回应我，我就去赢下游戏，把它带出去。
Page.LocalizedString:
The banquet was just a smokescreen. The real "game" was cruel beyond belief. I regretted coming to Fogden the moment I stepped inside, and all I could do was search everywhere for Inanna, swearing I'd use her blood to honor my companions—until I reached a valley. There, I found a mark my companions had left behind: "Eyes." That pattern was something Rio, our youngest, used to doodle, and Captain Zane adopted it as the group's emblem. Rio had an uncanny sense of direction. No matter where he was, he never got lost.

I followed the mark deeper in and saw a massive serpent creature. Before I could even react, it let out a mournful cry and retreated deeper into the cave. Along the way, I saw the remains of other people—it would attack everyone else, but it never once attacked me.

I chased it all the way to the end of the valley and cornered it. For the first time, it turned back to face me. On the serpent's head was Renita's face. Its jaws and cries resembled Orion's voice. The butterfly-like scale-wings were exactly like the ones by Tsubaki's ear. The structure of its body was like Zane's weapon. And those eye patterns covering its whole body… Rio, was that your doodle? You never found your way home again, then…

I'm going to try talking to it. If it still has the mind of a human, if it can still answer me, then I'll win the game and get it out of here.

Wuchao_Daff_Report_01.Comment: 达夫蒂尔部分碎片信息

Page.SourceString:
兄鉴，来信收悉。

父亲若还在世，看到你顶着长子的身份把他的家业变卖，扭头就跟那些所谓的贵人去做什么一本万利的买卖，最后还赔个精光，怕是连眼都闭不上。对了，你离开之后，母亲被气得进了医院，至今还躺在病床上。她有套首饰
是外公传下的，她说值些钱，叫我们拿去典当了，好让我和妹妹能继续念书。我怀着侥幸的心回家打开保险柜，呵，空的。知道密码的除了父母就是你，你离家之前拿走了一切值钱的东西，一个子儿也没给我们留。

我会给你一周的时间，你要么回到家跟我们好好谈谈，要么就等着，我会让妹妹改名换姓寄宿去远房亲戚家，然后公开你的行径让你身败名裂。
Page.LocalizedString:
Brother, I received your letter.

If Father were still alive and witnessed you, his eldest son, selling off the family estate, only to then turn around and be led on by those so-called bigwigs into some pyramid scheme, only to lose everything to your name, he'd probably die on the spot all over again. Another thing: after you left, Mother was so furious she ended up in the hospital. She's still there to this day. She had a set of jewelry
passed down from Grandfather. She said it was worth something and told us to pawn it, so our sister and I could keep going to school. I came home with a sliver of hope and opened the safe. Empty. The only people who knew the combination were Father, Mother, and you. Before you left, you took every last valuable thing in the house and didn't leave us a single cent.

I'll give you one week. Either come home and talk this through with us, or wait and see—I'll have sister sent to distant relatives under a new name, then expose everything you've done and make sure you're completely ruined for the rest of your days.

实验记录

雾巢会侵蚀歧骸的心智。不同种类的歧骸在进入后逐渐失去原有的行动逻辑，开始无差别攻击同类。伊南娜没有骗我——直接投入歧骸无法形成有效战力，需要寻找其他途径。
Page.LocalizedString:
Experiment Record

The Fogden erodes the minds of Oddities. Once inside, different types of Oddities lose their normal behavior patterns, stop acting like themselves, and begin attacking their own kind indiscriminately. Inanna didn't lie—deploying Oddities directly won't produce an effective fighting force. We need to find another approach.

Wuchao_Daff_Report_03.Comment: 达夫蒂尔部分碎片信息

Page.SourceString:
亲爱的怀仁博士：

听闻您因实验伦理问题被剥夺一切学术职务与资格，我深感惋惜。一群坐井观天的庸人，如何能理解您所探寻的真理？
您曾拒绝过我的邀请。但我看得出，您对雾柩本身的兴趣，远胜过对我的戒备。既然如此，何不借此机会亲自来雾巢看一看，权当散心？我会为您备好您需要的一切——包括一份千金难求的异象契约。这里没有评审会，没有禁令，只有灼灼真理。

盼复。

伊南娜敬上
Page.LocalizedString:
Darling Dr. Huairen,

I was deeply saddened to hear that experimental ethics violations have cost you all your academic posts and qualifications. How could a bunch of parochial mediocrities ever understand your work?
You once declined my invitation, but I can see that your interest in the Fog Coffin itself far outweighs your wariness of me. In that case, why not come to Fogden yourself and investigate, if only to settle your worries? I will have everything you need ready—including an Anomaly Contract that money can scarcely buy. There are no review boards here, no prohibitions—only the raw truth, uncovered.

I look forward to your reply.

Respectfully yours, Inanna

I can't afford my high medical costs, but I also couldn't bear to make the person I love wait for someone who's dying, so I came here.

When you arrive with nothing, yet Inanna still treats you like a guest of honor, that means something's up. You'd have to have something of value for her to even consider you—something she could squeeze out of you, like an Esper Ability.

我和剩下两名组员辉环收集完成，出现面具和大雾。特蕾莎先进入雾中探索，有绑上救生绳，但很快那边就没了动静。尼诺执意要去雾中找特蕾莎，我抓好绳子这头，他顺着绳子进入雾中。没过多久我能感觉到绳子那头像失去了牵引，软软地垂了下来。任凭我怎么晃动绳子，那边也没有任何反应。

Page.LocalizedString:
Squad 7 Group B Operational Log
Recorder: J
The two remaining team members and I finished collecting our Lumen Circles, when masks and thick fog suddenly appeared. Teresa went into the fog first to scout with a rope tied onto her, but before long there was no sound or movement. Nino was dead set on going into the fog to find Teresa and get her out. I gripped the rope tightly while he followed it into the fog. Not long after, I could feel the rope on the far end lose its pull and hang there, slack. No matter how much I shook it, there was no response from the other side.

This is an investigation with no way back. I will remain here on standby, awaiting the others.

ShadowChase_GameplayTips_001.Comment: 无影灯异象玩法的介绍

Title.SourceString: 关于附近区域电路维修的通知：
Title.LocalizedString: Notice of Electrical Repairs in the Area:

Page.SourceString:
该区域电路因不明异象原因遭到损坏，正在维修中。电力维修人员检查后确认故障发生时间为晚8点至早5点之间，请远离绕行。
异象管理局提醒您：异象会以阴影的姿态出现。若被该异象缠住难以脱身，请勿惊慌失措，普通市民不要尝试与其周旋。应在阴影消失的间隙，远离异常路灯。或尝试使用照明设备对其阴影进行驱散后，离开现场。
警告各位异象猎人，该异象会以黑雾的形式在路灯间进行窜逃。若能力不济者，切勿盲目追击，以免落入陷阱。
如您需要帮助或有想要提供的线索，请及时联系海特洛异象管理局。
Page.LocalizedString:
Electrical infrastructure in this area has been damaged by an unidentified Anomaly and is currently undergoing repairs. Maintenance personnel have confirmed that the disturbances occur between 8:00 PM and 5:00 AM. Members of the public are advised to avoid the affected area and use alternate routes.
The Bureau of Anomaly Control advises that this Anomaly manifests in the form of a shadow. If you become entangled and are unable to break free, remain calm. Civilians should not attempt to confront or evade the Anomaly directly. When the shadow recedes, move away from any affected streetlights. Alternatively, use a suitable light source to disperse the shadow before leaving the area.
All Anomaly Hunters are advised that the Anomaly can assume the form of black mist and move rapidly between streetlights. Those without sufficient capability should not pursue it recklessly, as doing so may result in entrapment.
If you require assistance or have relevant information to report, please contact the Hethereau Bureau of Anomaly Control without delay.

经过审判官的裁决，玛格达·穆勒无罪，不幸溺亡后，财产将由她的儿子帕勒姆·穆勒和萨莉·穆勒继承。
Page.LocalizedString:
…Midwife Magda Müller, her hands bound, was cast into the Luther River by Matthew Hopkins. She did not rise for a considerable while; the blessed waters received her, thereby proving the purity of her soul.
By the inquisitor's verdict, Magda Müller was innocent. Upon her unfortunate drowning, her property shall pass to her children, Parham Müller and Sally Müller.

Title.SourceString: 马修·霍普金斯的猎巫手记残页

Page.SourceString:
新月后的第二日，桃乐茜·奥斯本被指控与恶魔勾结，我将她全身的毛发剃光，终于在头顶发现了三颗痣，那正是魔鬼给她留下的印记！她拒不承认，就如所有恶魔的代行者一般。但这可难不倒我，我太懂得如何让他们俯首认罪！
连续五日失去睡眠后，她已经无力狡辩，谎言终于告破，她承认了自己在恶魔的黑皮书上签下血字，她就是魔女！她承认了，她来到卡斯科村，是在给敌国的士兵带路，让异教徒染指这片荒原，她让冻土不化，让瘟疫肆虐，让卡斯科人忍饥挨饿，她用占卜的魔法扭曲人们的信仰，引诱人们堕落，她就是魔女！
Page.LocalizedString:
On the second day after the new moon, Dorothy Osborne was accused of consorting with the Devil. I shaved every hair from her body and finally found three moles atop her head—three marks of sin, the Devil's own marks! She refused to confess, as was common with many servants of the Devil. Alas, that did not trouble me. I knew exactly how to make them bow their heads and confess!
After five consecutive days without sleep, she was too weak to keep up her denials. At last, her lies were exposed. She confessed to signing the Devil's black book in blood. She was a witch! She confessed that she had come to Casco to guide the enemy, allowing heretics to set foot upon this wasteland. She kept the frozen earth from thawing, unleashed pestilence, and left the Cascans starving. She used divination magic to twist the people's faith and lure them into depravity. She was a witch!

Title.SourceString: 马修·霍普金斯的猎巫手记残页2

Page.SourceString: 满月后的第六日，玛格达·穆勒为农妇艾尔莎·厄休拉接生，这是她今年接生的十二个孩子，也是卡斯科村第15个死婴。过去的一年半里，她接生的孩子，没有一个活下来，她一定是个魔女！只要成功清除她，就是我在这个村子找到的第五个魔女了！加上这五个银币，我今年赚到的赏金已经足足有八百一十银币，已经和去年赚得一样多了！这才刚过秋分！
Page.LocalizedString: On the sixth day after the full moon, Magda Müller served as midwife for Elsa Ursula, a peasant woman. That makes twelve children she has delivered this year—and Casco's fifteenth stillborn baby. Not a single child she has delivered over the past year and a half has survived. She must be a witch! If I successfully purge her, she'll be the fifth witch I've found in this village! With these five silver coins, my bounty earnings for the year have reached a whopping eight hundred and ten silver coins—already as much as I earned last year! And it's only just past the autumn equinox!

Title.SourceString: 马修·霍普金斯的猎巫手记残页3

Page.SourceString: 我的刀和针已经让整个村子都害怕我了，人人都要尊称我一声魔女将军，唯独玛格达·穆勒不同，她不害怕我的针和刀，拒不认罪，她小瞧我了！我用夹棍夹紧她的手指，用针撬开她的指甲，用荆棘鞭打她，让我的助手日夜围在她的身边哭嚎，她总算是尊敬我了！可她依然不承认自己和恶魔勾结，将那些婴孩的灵魂送给恶魔换取魔法，我只能让圣洁的水检验她了！
Page.LocalizedString: My knives and needles have made the entire village fear me. Every soul calls me the Master Witch-Hunter—but Magda Müller is different. She does not fear my needles or knives, and refuses to confess. She has underestimated me! I clamped her fingers in the thumbscrew, pried up her fingernails with needles, whipped her with a thorned lash, and had my assistants surround her day and night. At last, she respected me! Yet she still would not admit to consorting with the Devil and offering infants' souls to him in exchange for magic. I had no choice but to test her with holy water!

Title.SourceString: 被踩踏的审判记录残页

Page.SourceString:
……多人指控外来者猎巫人马修·霍普金斯与恶魔勾结，他双手被缚，由帕勒姆·穆勒丢入路德河中，圣洁的水拒绝了他，神明告诉我们，他是个与恶魔勾结的邪恶之徒。
经过审判官的裁决，男巫他虽已认罪，但他的灵魂堕落太久，神明也不能宽恕他。下一个满月，马修·霍普金斯将被处以火刑。
Page.LocalizedString:
…Many have accused the outsider witch-hunter Matthew Hopkins of consorting with the Devil. His hands were bound, and Parham Müller cast him into the Luther River. The holy water rejected him, and the Highest One showed us the truth: he was in league with the Devil.
By the inquisitor's judgment, although the sinful warlock had confessed, his soul had fallen too far, and even the Highest One could not forgive him. At the next full moon, Matthew Hopkins was to be burned at the stake.

Page.SourceString:
亲爱的莱利：
你们的离开恐怕是对的，日子越来越不太平了。不光是巡查治安官，我在放牛的时候，竟然在荒原的边缘，看到了邻国的士兵。好在我跑得快，没有被他们瞧见。国王战败的消息恐怕是真的，也不知道他们会不会闯进卡斯科来。洪水越来越频繁，恐怕邻国的日子也不好过，我有些担心他们会来村里抢走我们的粮食。
你们在南方的镇子过得还好吗？那边会不会暖和些，土地会不会更容易种活小麦？我最近已经开始在变卖财产，或许很快就要去投奔你们了。如果你们的日子过得艰难，也请不要担心袒露实情，我可以另寻他处。若是我能找到更好的地方安顿，便和你们联络，总之我会向更南边去，找块更温暖和肥沃的土地。
随信附上我新的占卜结果，或许对……
Page.LocalizedString:
Dear Riley,
You were right to depart, I fear. The times grow less peaceful with each passing day. It is not the patrol constables alone. While I was out with the cattle, I beheld soldiers of the neighboring kingdom at the very edge of the moor. By the mercy of the Highest One, I am swift of foot, and they did not spy me. The tidings of the King's defeat are like enough to be true, and none can say whether they will press into Casco. The floods come ever more often, and I doubt not our neighbors suffer likewise, I am half afraid they will fall upon the village and take our grain.
How do you fare in your town to the south? Is it warmer there? Does the land more readily bear wheat? I have already begun to sell off what I own, and may come to cast my lot with you before long. If your own days are hard, I pray you do not fear to tell me the truth, for I can seek elsewhere. Should I find a better place to settle, I will send word. Either way, I am bound further south, to seek out warmer and richer land.
I have enclosed with this letter my latest divination. Perhaps it may…

Page.SourceString:
>YYYYYY

>昨天游戏进程还能正常运行的今天为什么报错了你快帮我进文件夹里看一下
>是不是你昨晚关掉之后把文件拆出来看的时候不小心动到然后手贱按了保存啊
>我打算研究下那个武器的隐藏数值嘛，机制也有一点不清楚的，知道是哪个就没问题了代码本身我背下来了
>虽然我用Y之手也能修好，但你这脑子也像是有特异功能一样好BUG的说

Page.LocalizedString:
>YYYYYY

Page.SourceString:
>我在想，我们能永远这样在一起玩吗，Y？
>大概不能吧，你看就算是再耐玩的可以无限随机生成的游戏，还是被我们玩腻了

>那也不会是永远的，等你以后上班工作了，你就没时间回来这里找我了

>哈哈哈你不反对我就当你同意了

>hahaha you didn't say no so that's a yes in my book

Page.SourceString:
Y，该说是我的网友吗？
这台电脑也没法联网，在离线的情况下和一个电脑里的朋友交流，还是该说本地友？电子友？
之前有吐嘈过Y还特地弄了张貌似在走可爱路线的角色贴图充当自己界面形象，实际上完全是个胡闹的家伙嘛！
当然也有奇怪的地方就是了，没有网络也就搜索不了网图，是从哪里搞到的素材？什么游戏里的吗？
耳朵是尖尖的，奇幻故事里的那种精灵，一般是长生种的设定吧却又是个小孩，还穿着像是来自校园题材作品的校服。
emmm猜不太出来这游戏的背景啊，总之八成，是Y中意的某个虚拟角色吧？
算了不纠结，Y就是Y。
Page.LocalizedString:
I mean, I guess Y is my online buddy?
This rig can't even go online. If I'm talking to a friend inside it, all offline, doesn't that make them my local or digital buddy?
I gave Y a hard time before. They went out of their way to slap on some cutesy sticker as their avatar. Turns out they're a total goofball!
Still kinda weird though. There's no internet, so they can't just grab images off the web. Then where did they even get the art? Was it ripped from some game?
Look at the pointed ears, like the elves in fantasy stuff. Those are usually the immortal types that live forever. But this one's a kid, and they're wearing something like a school uniform straight out of some high school anime.
Hmm, can't really place what game this is from. Anyway, I bet it's some virtual character Y is into.
Whatever, not gonna overthink it. Y is who Y is.

Page.SourceString:
Y在我带来的那部新发售的格斗游戏里，给我们双方各捏了一个定制化的英雄！
酷毙了！！！而且100%匹配我们各自偏好。
我想要的是不受束缚，逍遥自在的射手类型的英雄！有种游走在灰色地带的自由者调调真不错。
Y那边则是设计成了公权机构的铁血社会人，一个认真负责有礼貌的工作狂战士，我会觉得有点没劲啦，但Y喜欢就好。
某种程度上也确实契合，说教的时候偶尔会戴上眼镜的感觉哈哈！
对了，之后让Y把这两个英雄也挪到别的游戏当成可用角色来玩，好像是个好主意！
Page.LocalizedString:
Y built us each a custom hero in that new fighting game I brought over!
So friggin' cool!!! And they totally nailed what each of us likes.
I wanted a ranged type, unchained and free-roaming! I love that vibe, a free spirit drifting through the gray zone.
Y went the other way and made a hardcore company person from some government agency. They're a serious, dutiful, polite workaholic warrior. I find the character a bit boring, but hey, whatever Y likes.
Gotta admit the character somewhat fits them. They even put on glasses when they start lecturing, hah!
Oh, and here's a great idea: I should get Y to port these two heroes into other games as playable characters!

Page.SourceString:
致敬爱的黑羽小姐，
这里有很多人需要您的帮助。世上只有您能够拯救他们，非您不可！事态复杂且棘手，难以在信中详细说明，但您只要来看上一眼就会明白有多严重。请您看在这么多人急切等待您的份上，务必发些善心，帮帮我！如果您不能前来，我真的不知道接下来该怎么办了！请您帮帮我吧！帮帮我吧！请您务必帮帮我吧！
您的梅露菈
Page.LocalizedString:
Dear Blackbird,
Many souls here need your help. In all the world, you alone can save them. You must help them! The matter is tangled and grievous, more than I can say within a letter, but you need only come and look once to see how dire it is. I beg you, for the sake of all these many souls who wait upon you eagerly, take pity and help me! If you cannot come, I truly know not what I am to do next! I beg you, help me! Help me! I beg you, help!
Yours, Merula

Page.SourceString: 有个特殊的孩子迷失在了这里，请你带它回家吧。
Page.LocalizedString: A special child is lost here. Please find them and take them home.

Page.SourceString: 别怕别转头，孩子们都是你的朋友。
Page.LocalizedString: Don't be afraid. Don't turn around. The children are all your friends.

Page.SourceString: 这里的孩子们很害羞，看不见它们时才会移动。
Page.LocalizedString: The children here are very shy. They only move when you aren't looking at them.

Page.SourceString: 特殊的孩子不一样，它太活泼调皮，不多看着点可不行。
Page.LocalizedString: This special child is different. They're far too lively and playful—you can't afford to take your eyes off them.

Page.LocalizedString: Look at me! Look at me! Can't we get you to look at us?

Page.SourceString:
「序言」
《魔女之槌》由首都裁判所审判官海因里希·克拉梅与大司铎雅各布·司布伦格合著，获得了国王的认可与赞许，做为狩猎魔女的指南在全国发售，以指引地方司铎和信众们如何识别与审判魔女。
魔女是第一个在恶魔之书上签下姓名的女巫，是众巫之首，是地下之国的王后。邪恶的女巫，个个都想成为魔女，个个效仿魔女，因此无论是女巫还是魔女，都一样是恶魔的爪牙，真正的祸害。
无法满足的欲望促使一个人与魔鬼合谋，进而堕落，灵魂被献祭换来魔法。而女人的灵魂尤为脆弱，她们不懂思考与判断，因此容易滋生欲望，更容易受魔鬼操纵，她们是友谊的敌人、注定的处罚、必定的罪恶、天生的诱惑、勾引人的灾难、家庭的威胁、迷人的祸害。为了抗衡魔鬼的力量，诸位更需谨言慎行，坚守道德，捍卫名声；任何不寻常的言行，任何德行有失，都可能是恶魔悄然临近的征兆。观察你的女邻居，观察你的女儿，观察你的妻子，观察你身边的每一个人，任何灵魂都可能在恶魔的操控下沦为魔女。若是有人不相信恶魔和魔女，那此人必是最大的异端！
为了守护神明的信众们，请诸位认真阅读本书，以学习如何辨别魔女，如何识别道德堕落的灵魂，如何识别异端与法术；若是诸位担心自己已经着魔或是被诅咒，可以在本书中学习如何破除魔法；审判官和司铎们亦可以在本书中习得审判魔女的手段和程序。
我们虔诚地向神明祈求，让书中的知识在所有信众间传扬，为了对抗狡猾的恶魔，我们绝不放过任何一个可能是魔女之人！绝不放过任何恶魔的代行者！坚决守护神明的荣耀！
Page.LocalizedString:
"Preface"
The Hexenhammer was written together by Heinrich Kramer, Inquisitor of the Capital Tribunal, and Jacob Sprenger, High Confessor. Having received the King's approval and commendation, it was sent forth through all the kingdom as a guide unto the hunting of the Witch, that the Confessors of every parish and the faithful might learn to know and to judge the Witch.
The Witch was the first among hags to set her name within the Devil's book. She is the foremost of all witches, the Queen of the world below. Every wicked hag doth desire to become a witch, and every one of them fashioneth herself after the Witch. And thus are hag and witch alike the very talons of the Devil, a true and present scourge.
Insatiable desire driveth a soul to conspire with the Devil and so to fall, the soul offered up in exchange for magic. And a woman's soul is weaker still, for women know not how to reason or to judge, and thus doth desire take root in them easily, and they are the more readily worked upon by the Devil. They are the enemy of friendship, an inescapable punishment, a certain evil, a natural temptation, a beckoning calamity, a threat unto the household, a bewitching scourge. To stand against the power of the Devil, ye must all be the more careful in word and deed, holding fast unto virtue and guarding your good name. Any strange word or act, any failing in virtue, may be a sign that the Devil draweth quietly near. Watch thy woman neighbor, watch thy daughter, watch thy wife, watch every soul about thee, for any soul may fall beneath the Devil's hand and become a witch. And whosoever will not believe in the Devil and in the Witch, that one is the greatest heretic of all!
For the protection of the faithful, let all of ye read this book with care, that ye may learn how to tell a witch, how to know a soul fallen into corruption, how to discern heresy and sorcery. And shouldst thou fear that thou thyself art possessed or cursed, thou mayest learn from this book how to break such magic. Inquisitors and Confessors, too, may learn from it the means and the procedures for the judging of witches.
We pray devoutly to the Highest One that the knowledge in this book may spread among all the faithful. To fight against the cunning of the Devil, we will let slip no one who may be a witch! We will let slip no agent of the Devil! We will defend the glory of the Highest One without wavering!

Page.SourceString:
「魔女和恶魔的交易」
恶魔有这一本黑熊皮毛装订的黑皮书，书页带着暗红色的光泽，记录了魔鬼的各种法术和它的真名。恶魔的代行者们会用灵魂抵押，以鲜血作墨在书上签下姓名，交换来自己梦寐以求的魔法。交易一旦成功，魔女们永远不可能放弃，这意味着她们的灵魂无法被拯救，只有死亡可以终结她们给神明的信众们带来的诅咒。
每个满月时分，魔女们会在背上涂抹飞行药膏，骑着扫把前往山顶参加「魔女会」。魔女们点燃黑蜡烛召唤恶魔，恶魔便化身黑山羊出现，林间满是她们的祝颂恶魔歌声与游戏声；在狂欢中，她们烤动物的肉作美食，献祭婴儿给魔鬼，换来巨大的力量诅咒善良的灵魂。
她们使寒冷降临，让土地结冻再也无法种植庄稼，从而让饥饿遍布大地；她们使用草药诅咒河水，沿着河流散布瘟疫，让死亡充斥人间；她们用绳结和动物的骨头施法增加力量，魅惑身边的每一个人，传播邪恶的欲望，最终诱使更多的灵魂堕落，她们是罪的使者。
Page.LocalizedString:
"The Bargain Between Witch and Devil"
The Devil keeps a book bound in the hide of a black bear, its pages carrying a dark red sheen, wherein are set down his every sorcery and his true name. The Devil's servants pledge their souls, and with blood for ink they sign their names in the book, receiving in exchange the magic they have so long craved. Once the bargain is struck, the witches can never turn back, which means their souls can no longer be saved, and death alone can end the curse they bring upon the faithful.
At every full moon, the witches spread flying ointment upon their backs and ride their brooms to the mountaintop to join the Witches' Sabbath. They light black candles to summon the Devil, and the Devil appears in the shape of a black goat. The woods fill with their songs of praise to him and the sounds of their games. In the frenzy they roast the flesh of animals for their feast, and offer infants in sacrifice to the Devil, receiving in exchange great power to curse the souls of the good.
We pray devoutly unto the Highest One that the knowledge within this book may spread among all the faithful. To war against the cunning of the Devil, we will let slip no one who may be a witch! We will let slip no agent of the Devil! We will defend the glory of the Highest One without wavering!

Page.SourceString:
「魔女的特征」
魔女的灵魂早就堕落，所以常常过着不道德的生活，玷污自己的名声；如果遇到一个虔诚而端庄的魔女，那恐怕是狡猾在起作用，她想用伪装出的虔诚和道德来迷惑你，以免被怀疑。
那些刚刚献祭灵魂的魔女，常常还有残存的道德和良心，会在接受审问时露出恐惧，恐惧绝望、垂头丧气，缄默不语，这就足以说明她背叛神明犯下严重的罪行。
如果她自称无罪，保持镇静，那么显然是恶魔的法术在保护她不露出马脚，这足以证明她的罪行。
若是老道的魔女，最擅长撒谎和欺骗，她们毫不吝惜地胡言乱语着，全力辩驳，那是着魔的表现，与恶魔越是亲近的人便越容易着魔，她必然是有罪的。
不要放过魔女的蛛丝马迹，那些被缚住手脚的魔女，最喜欢在受刑的时候转动眼睛，那是她在利用眼神给恶魔送信，要小心，她可能因此多挺住一天的刑罚，但只要带着神明的意志坚持下去，恶魔也无法一直帮助她。
若是魔女在认罪前断气，不要害怕，立刻请求司铎的帮助，举行驱魔仪式；因为那死亡是恶魔带来的，魔女想要向神明坦诚自己的罪过，但恶魔不允许她说出更多的名单和秘密，行刑人若是恐惧死亡，便会在此时堕落，务必保持勇气和坚定的信仰，相信神明会保护你，以意志守护灵魂，以虔诚对抗恶魔。
Page.LocalizedString:
"The Marks of a Witch"
The soul of a witch hath long since fallen, and so doth she often live an immoral life and stain her own good name. Shouldst thou meet a witch who seemeth devout and modest, it is likely her cunning at work, for she meaneth to deceive thee with a pretended piety and virtue, that she may escape suspicion.
Those witches who have but lately offered up their souls often keep some remnant of morality and conscience, and under questioning they show their fear, they are afraid, they despair, they hang their heads and fall silent, and this alone is proof enough that they have betrayed the Highest One and committed grievous sins.
If they claim to be innocent and stay calm, then plainly it is the Devil's sorcery that protecteth them from betraying themselves, and this is proof enough of their guilt.
As for seasoned witches, they are most skilled of all at lying and deceiving. They pour out wild falsehoods without restraint and argue back with all their strength. These are signs of possession, for the closer they are unto the Devil, the more easily are they possessed, and they must be guilty.
Let no faint trace escape thee. Those witches whose hands and feet are bound love above all to roll their eyes amid the torture, for they are using their gaze to send word unto the Devil. Take care, for by this they may hold out against the punishment a day longer, but so long as thou pressest on with the will of the Highest One, the Devil cannot help them forever.
Should a witch draw her last breath before confessing, fear not. Call at once for the aid of a Confessor, and hold the rite of exorcism, for that death was brought by the Devil. The witch wished to confess her sins unto the Highest One, but the Devil would not suffer her to speak more of the names and secrets. The executioner who feareth death will fall into corruption at this moment. Thou must keep thy courage and thy steadfast faith, trusting that the Highest One will protect thee, guarding thy soul with thy will and standing against the Devil with thy devotion.

Page.SourceString:
「识破魔女的伪装！」
与恶魔勾结的魔女，身上必定会留下恶魔的印记。恶魔和魔女是狡猾的，只有剃光魔女身上全身的毛发，一寸一厘仔细搜寻，才能发现；恶魔的印记尝尝伪装成痣、雀斑、胎记、被虫咬的包或者疤痕，以方便魔女狡辩，请提高警惕，切勿被蒙骗！切勿！
「魔女的魔宠」
魔女为了方便给神明的信众们下咒，不得不掩藏行踪，所以她们喜欢饲养魔宠，例如狼、兔、鸟、蛤蟆、猫、龟、猪、刺猬和羊等等，小心饲养了动物的任何女人！
「魔女的眼泪」
堕落的灵魂无法感到悲伤，所以魔女无法流下眼泪。但是恶魔教会她们流泪的法术，所以当她们被审问和受刑时，常常利用法术伪装流泪，那是恶魔在帮她们伪装哭泣，骗取你的同情，小心不要被她们蒙骗！
Page.LocalizedString:
"See Through the Disguise of the Witch!"
The witch who hath made her pact with the Devil will surely bear upon her body the Devil's mark. The Devil and the witch are cunning, and only by shaving away every hair upon the witch's body and searching inch by inch shall it be found. Oftentimes the Devil's mark disguiseth itself as a mole, a freckle, a birthmark, an insect's bite, or a scar, that the witch may argue her way free. Be ever watchful, and suffer not thyself to be deceived! Suffer it not!
"The Wicked Familiar of the Witch"
That she may the more easily lay her curses upon the faithful, the witch must hide her tracks, and so she loveth to keep a familiar, such as a wolf, a hare, a bird, a toad, a cat, a tortoise, a swine, a hedgehog, a sheep, and the like. Beware any woman who keepeth an animal!
"The Tears of the Witch"
A fallen soul can feel no sorrow, and so the witch cannot weep true tears. But the Devil hath taught them the sorcery of weeping, and so, when they are questioned and put to torture, they oftentimes feign tears by this sorcery. It is the Devil helping them to counterfeit their weeping, that they may cheat thee of thy pity. Take care thou art not deceived by them!

Title.SourceString:
《魔女之锤》
第二部分（第154页）

Page.SourceString:
「魔女的克星」
恶魔是伟大神明的敌人，水与火都是神明的神圣造物，最适合验证一个灵魂是否已经堕落。
若是魔女，被投入水中时，神圣的水会拒绝接纳堕落的灵魂，排斥魔女的存在，因此魔女会浮在水面上；若是灵魂足够虔诚，便会沉入水底，但要小心，狡猾的魔女可能使用法术假装沉底；但神圣的水会耗尽魔力，所以需要在水边等待足够的时间，才能确定一个灵魂是不是已经堕落，千万要有耐心！
若是魔女，走过被神圣之火烧红的铁面时，必然会发出痛苦的哀嚎；等待三日后，伤口会呈现被神圣之火净化过的样子，这样便可确定魔女的存在。
Page.LocalizedString:
"The Bane of the Witch"
The Devil is the enemy of the Highest One. Both water and fire are His holy works, most fit to prove whether a soul hath fallen.
If she be a witch, then when cast into the water, the holy water will refuse to receive her fallen soul and will cast her out, and so the witch will float upon the surface. If the soul be devout enough, it will sink beneath the water. But take care, for the cunning witch may use her sorcery to feign sinking. Yet the holy water will wear her magic away, and so thou must wait a sufficient time at the water's edge before thou canst be certain whether a soul hath fallen. Whatever befalleth, have patience!
If she be a witch, then when she walketh across the iron plate made red by the holy fire, she will surely let forth a wail of anguish. After three days' waiting, the wound will show itself cleansed by the holy fire, and thus may the witch be known for certain.

Title.SourceString:
《魔女之锤》
第三部分（第185页）

Page.SourceString:
「魔女的恶行」
魔女把公牛溺死在水里，让牛跳离地面四英尺多高，把长柄锅扔进火里，把干草倾倒出运货的马车，给啤酒施上魔法，击碎提桶又让水壶跳起舞来。她们在空中投掷苹果、椅子、灰烬、烛台和粪便。她们放出没有躯干的邪恶生物，人头白猫尾，躯干竟空空如也。
魔女能同时出现于两地，也能走过潮湿的路段却依然浑身干燥。哪怕走在松动的地板上，她们也能做到悄无声息。他们还可以火速到达一个地方，占卜出未开信件的内容，制作异常美味的奶酪，滞销漂白不批的奥秘，闻到他人口袋中的无花果味，从楼顶摔下后却毫发无伤。
人被魔女施咒后，可能失去知觉，四肢瘫痪，全身痉挛，张口卡顿；有人也会口吐白沫，紧咬牙关，身体抽搐难止。
Page.LocalizedString:
"The Evil Deeds of the Witch"
The witch drowneth the bull in the water, and maketh the ox leap more than four feet from the ground. She casteth the long-handled pot into the fire, tippeth the hay out from the wagon, layeth her magic upon the ale, shattereth the pail and setteth the kettle to dancing. She hurleth through the air apples, chairs, ashes, candlesticks, and dung. She looseth forth wicked creatures without bodies: a man's head upon a white cat's tail, the trunk of them empty as air.
The witch can appear in two places at once, and can walk a wet stretch of road yet stay dry from head to foot. Even upon a loose and creaking floor she maketh not a sound. She can reach a place in all haste, divine the contents of an unopened letter, make cheese of an uncommon savor, know secrets not meant to be known, smell the figs within another's pocket, and fall from a rooftop yet take no hurt at all.
One upon whom the witch hath laid her curse may lose all sense, his limbs struck useless, his whole body seized with convulsions, his mouth locked fast. Some too will foam at the mouth, their teeth clenched tight, their bodies wracked with fits that will not cease.

Title.SourceString:
《魔女之锤》
第三部分（第222页）

Page.SourceString:
「魔女审判」
为了守护神明的荣耀，为了驱赶恶魔，阻止灾难和瘟疫的蔓延。在司铎皇的指引下，国王下令设立神圣裁判所。并专门培训一百名职业的魔女审判官。
神圣裁判所的使命
经过培训后的审判官们，掌握了最多的鉴别魔女的技巧，他们将会在全国巡回，尽可能找出潜藏的魔女。
同时，经过司铎认可的魔女猎人们，也拥有鉴别魔女的能力，如果其拥有足够的证据，可先处决魔女，随后带着证据领取赏金。
若是某一村落或城镇发现魔女的征兆，或是有其他恶魔代行者的踪迹，但无法辨别，可以在当地司铎的指导下向临近的神圣裁判所申请一名审判官，裁判所将尽快派出审判官前往当地举行魔女审判。
Page.LocalizedString:
"The Trials of the Witch"
For the sake of the Highest One, for the sake of casting out the Devil, and for the sake of preventing calamities and plagues: under the guidance of the Papal Confessor, the King hath decreed the founding of the Holy Tribunal, and hath commanded that a hundred Inquisitors be trained to judge witches.
"The Mission of the Holy Tribunal"
The Inquisitors, once their training is done, will have mastered the greatest store of skills for the discerning of witches, and they will go in circuit through all the kingdom to seek out, so far as they may, every witch that lieth hidden.
At the same time, those witch-hunters approved by a Confessor likewise possess the power to discern witches, and should one hold proof enough, he may put witches to death first and thereafter bring his proof to claim bounty.
Should any village or town find the signs of a witch, or the traces of some other agent of the Devil, yet be unable to know them for certain, they may, under the guidance of their local Confessor, petition the nearest Holy Tribunal for an Inquisitor, and the Tribunal will send forth an Inquisitor with all haste to hold a witch trial in that place.

Title.LocalizedString: Chronicle of St. Arbor — The Fran Family

Page.SourceString:
建镇后的第214年，法勒·弗兰和莱西·弗兰诞下威尔·弗兰；
建镇后的第221年，蒲公英花盛开时，莱西·弗兰病逝；
建镇后的第236年，接生妇薇薇安·琼与女儿丽贝卡·琼受司铎乔治的邀请来到镇上，暂住在弗兰医生的诊所内
建镇后的第237年，爱丽丝·帕里斯难产，薇薇安和丽贝卡帮助了她，母子平安，加西亚镇长和乔治司铎嘉奖了她们；
建镇后的第240年，第一场大雪后，薇薇安·琼去世；
建镇后的第241年，紫罗兰盛开时，威尔·弗兰迎娶丽贝卡·琼，丽贝卡·琼改名为丽贝卡·弗兰；
建镇后的第243年，新年后，法勒·弗兰去世，独子威尔·弗兰继承弗兰家的诊所；
建镇后的第245年，盛夏，丽贝卡·弗兰诞下安妮·弗兰；
建镇后的第260年，向日葵花开时，丽贝卡·弗兰和威尔·弗兰死于瘟疫；
根据遗嘱，在安妮成人前，弗兰家的遗产由司铎乔治和维克托镇长联合看管；
建镇后的第266年，司铎乔治与维克托镇长将弗兰夫妇留下的遗产交还安妮·弗兰；
安妮·弗兰收留了两名异乡人；

Title.LocalizedString: Chronicle of St. Arbor — The Wall Family

Page.SourceString:
建镇后的第227年，面包坊的主人英曼·沃尔的表亲，15岁的莱克·恩斯特来到沃尔家的面包坊中做学徒；
建镇后的第231年，紫罗兰盛开时，莱克·恩斯特迎娶邻镇的卡珊德拉·尼克劳斯，卡珊德拉·尼克劳斯改名卡珊德拉·恩斯特；
建镇后的第232年，第一声春雷来临那天，莱克·恩斯特收养了门口的弃婴，为其取名卡特·恩斯特；
建镇后的第233年，新年后，英曼·沃尔和凯特琳·沃尔诞下路易·沃尔；
建镇后的第234年，深冬，莱克·恩斯特未点蜡烛，死于地窖中；
建镇后的第235年，新年前，卡珊德拉·恩斯特难产，诞下她与莱克·恩斯特的女儿多特·恩斯特后逝世；
沃尔家收养了卡特·恩斯特与多特·恩斯特；
建镇后的第248年，新年后，卡特·恩斯特因欠赌债入狱，多特·恩斯特向沃尔家借钱支付债务后，卡特·恩斯特出狱；
初雪前，卡特·恩斯特因欠下赌债逃离镇子，投奔商队出海；
初雪后，英曼·沃尔病逝；
建镇后的第249年，新年前，卡特·恩斯特带着经商获利回到镇上，雇佣兰德·帕特南建造了酒馆；
多特·恩斯特开始去邻镇学习酿酒；
建镇后的第250年，盛夏，领主莱昂子爵一家出游，卡特·恩斯特在偷盗领主家的珠宝时被男仆发现，致男仆死亡，被判处绞刑；
建镇后的第252年，路易·沃尔迎娶多特·恩斯特，多特·恩斯特更名为多特·沃尔
建镇后的第254年，盛夏，路易·沃尔与多特·沃尔诞下怀特·沃尔，接生妇丽贝卡·弗兰；
最冷的雪天，怀特·沃尔病逝；
建镇后的第255年，新年前，凯特琳·沃尔病逝；
建镇后的第256年，初秋，路易·沃尔与多特·沃尔诞下爱丽丝·沃尔，接生妇丽贝卡·弗兰；
秋收时，爱丽丝·沃尔病逝；
建镇后的第258年，山楂花开时，路易·沃尔与多特·沃尔诞下玛丽·沃尔，接生妇丽贝卡·弗兰；
建镇后的第260年，秋收后，因怀疑磨坊私藏面粉，路易·沃尔起诉皮克托·科里，后经司铎乔治调节，二者言归于好；
建镇后的第262年，盛夏，沃尔家的酒馆因涉嫌盗贼销赃，被治安官查封；
秋收后，调查结束，沃尔家的酒馆重新开门；

Title.LocalizedString: Chronicle of St. Arbor — The Williams Family

Page.SourceString:
建镇后的第211年，新年后，洛哈特子爵将莱克山坡西面直到荆棘丛的土地抵押给莱昂子爵；附庸于这片土地的农奴克莱德·威廉和邦妮·威廉夫妇搬迁至圣阿尔博镇。
建镇后的第213年，克莱德与邦妮在镇西为领主放牧，约定以羊毛和乳酪的一部分折抵租赋；
建镇后的第219年，雏菊花盛开时，邦妮·威廉诞下约翰·威廉；
建镇后的第226年，入夏后，约翰开始跟随父亲放羊，熟悉山坡、溪流和通往森林的小路；
建镇后的第227年，新年后的第三天，邦妮·威廉诞下约瑟夫·威廉；
建镇后的第238年，约翰·威廉迎娶邻村的牧羊女维达·谢尔比，维达·谢尔比更名为维达·威廉；
建镇后的第240年，洪水来临时，克莱德·威廉为保护领主的羊群，失足跌入河中溺亡；
领主莱昂子爵奖励威廉一家土地，威廉一家不再是领主的农奴；
建镇后的第242年，约翰·威廉租得南面山坡草场的终身使用权；
建镇后的第246年，暴风雪中，约瑟夫·威廉为了寻回走丢的羊，右腿摔断；
建镇后的第256年，初春，因土地连年歉收，约翰·威廉将草场抵押给比利·帕特南，以放牧偿还利息；
建镇后的第260年，山楂花开时，约翰·威廉的堂兄斯科特·威廉死于瘟疫，斯科特·威廉之女阿比盖尔来到镇上投奔威廉一家；

Title.LocalizedString: Chronicle of St. Arbor — The Terry Family

Page.SourceString:
建镇后的第236年，初夏，老里维斯·特里与南希·特里诞下里维斯·特里；
建镇后的第241年，盛夏，老里维斯·特里与南希·特里诞下帕克·特里
建镇后的第245年，暮春，老里维斯·特里与南希·特里诞下帕梅拉·特里；
建镇后的第247年，积雪融化时，帕梅拉·特里死于天花；
建镇后的第254年，仲夏节，里维斯开始替村民修补犁头、马蹄铁和收割用的铁器；
建镇后的第257年，秋收后，特里家的弟弟也进入铁匠铺学徒，兄弟二人共同照看炉火；
建镇后的第260年，向日葵花开时，老里维斯·特里，南希·特里和帕克·特里死于瘟疫；
特里家的铁匠铺由里维斯·特里继承；

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第207年第15案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 15, 207 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：威尔·帕里斯与坎农·帕特南因二十条田的归属发生争执。
冬至时，威尔·帕里斯向庄园法庭控告坎农·帕特南拒绝归还二十条田。双方此前因借贷立下抵押约定，威尔以二十条田为抵押向坎农借取银币，并约定还清欠款后收回土地。
到期后，威尔虽迟了两日才还清欠款，仍要求收回抵押的田地。坎农则以其违约为由，拒绝归还。
裁断：
经莱昂子爵审理，庄园认定威尔·帕里斯已经偿清本金，二十条田仍归帕里斯家占有。但因威尔迟延还款，帕里斯家须另向帕特南家支付一月利息。
此后双方不得再以此二十条田相互争讼。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: A dispute between Will Parris and Cannon Putnam over the ownership of twenty strips of field.
At the winter solstice, Will Parris brought suit before the Manor Court against Cannon Putnam, that he had refused to return twenty strips of field. The two had beforehand entered into a covenant of mortgage upon a loan, wherein Will, putting up the twenty strips of field as pledge, borrowed silver coin of Cannon, and it was agreed that upon the clearing of the debt he should take back the land.
When the term was come, Will, though he was two days late in clearing the debt, did nonetheless demand the return of the pledged land. Cannon refused to return it, alleging that Will had broken the covenant.
Verdict:
Upon the hearing before Viscount Leon, the Manor findeth that Will Parris hath discharged the principal, and that the twenty strips of field remain in the holding of the Parris family. Yet because Will was late in his repayment, the Parris family must pay over unto the Putnam family one month's interest besides.
Hereafter neither party shall sue the other again for these twenty strips of field.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第224年第1案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 1, 224 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：帕特南家与帕里斯家因议婚宴上的争执发生斗殴。
新年时，兰德·帕特南与瑞雯·帕里斯议婚。双方家长在帕特南家的宴席上，因旧日土地纠纷和积怨再次发生争执，继而动手。
坎农·帕特南称，威尔·帕里斯在争斗中打伤自己，并损坏家中桌椅，遂请求庄园裁断。
裁断：
经查，双方均有过错。兰德·帕特南与瑞雯·帕里斯的议婚因此作罢。帕里斯家须赔付帕特南家桌椅的修缮费用，并承担坎农·帕特南因伤前往弗兰诊所所付的费用。
双方此后不得再借此次斗殴挑起旧日土地之争。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: An affray between the Putnam family and the Parris family, arising from a quarrel at a betrothal feast.
At the New Year, Rand Putnam and Raven Parris were to be betrothed. At the feast held in the Putnam house, the elders of both families, by reason of an old dispute over land and the grudges laid up therefrom, fell once more to quarreling, and thereafter to blows.
Cannon Putnam saith that Will Parris did wound him in the fray, and did damage the tables and chairs of the house, and thereupon prayed the judgment of the Manor.
Verdict:
Upon examination, it is found that both parties were at fault. The betrothal of Rand Putnam and Raven Parris is therefore broken off. The Parris family must make recompense unto the Putnam family for the mending of the tables and chairs, and must bear besides the charges paid by Cannon Putnam for going to Fran's apothecary on account of the injury.
Hereafter neither party shall, by occasion of this affray, stir up again the old dispute over land.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第225年第22案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 22, 225 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：维克托·帕里斯控告坎农·帕特南杀害其父威尔·帕里斯。
圣米格尔节后，威尔·帕里斯溺亡。维克托·帕里斯怀疑其父之死与坎农·帕特南有关，向庄园法庭提出控告。
因案件涉及人命，庄园法庭先将坎农·帕特南拘押，并将案件移交治安官进一步审理。
裁断：
经查，未发现坎农·帕特南谋害威尔·帕里斯的确实证据，坎农获释。
庄园法庭不再追究其杀人之罪，但将此案及审理经过记入簿册，以备日后查验。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Victor Parris accuseth Cannon Putnam of the killing of his father, Will Parris.
After Michaelmas, Will Parris was drowned. Victor Parris, suspecting that his father's death was linked to Cannon Putnam, brought his accusation before the Manor Court.
Forasmuch as the matter touched a man's life, the Manor Court first took Cannon Putnam into custody, and delivered the case unto the Constable for further hearing.
Verdict:
Upon examination, no sure proof was found that Cannon Putnam had murdered Will Parris, and Cannon was set free.
The Manor Court pursueth the charge of killing no further, yet hath entered this case and the course of its hearing into the record, that it may be examined in days to come.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第240年第11案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 11, 240 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：克莱德·威廉于履行领主劳役时溺亡，其家请求确认身后土地与身份。
洪水来临时，克莱德·威廉为保护领主莱昂子爵的羊群，冒雨赶羊渡河，不慎失足跌入河中溺亡。
其妻邦妮·威廉与儿子约翰·威廉失去一家之主。庄园查明，克莱德死于履行领主劳役期间，并无他人过错。
裁断：
莱昂子爵下令，赏赐威廉一家一片土地，以作抚恤。自此以后，威廉一家解除农奴身份，不再承担原先附属于土地的人身劳役。
此事记入庄园土地簿与户籍簿。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Clyde Williams was drowned in the doing of his lord's service, and his family seeketh confirmation of the land and standing they are to hold thereafter.
When the flood came, Clyde Williams, to safeguard the flock of his lord, Viscount Leon, drove the sheep across the river in the rain, and losing his footing unawares, fell into the river and was drowned.
His wife, Bonnie Williams, and his son, John Williams, were thus bereft of the head of their house. The Manor findeth that Clyde died in the doing of his lord's service, and that no other was at fault therein.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon commandeth that a parcel of land be bestowed upon the Williams family, as a solace and recompense. From this time forth, the Williams family are released from their bondage as serfs, and shall no longer bear the personal labor service formerly annexed unto the land.
This matter is entered into the Manor's land book and the roll of households.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第242年第2案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 2, 242 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：约翰·威廉请求取得镇南山坡草场的终身使用权。
约翰·威廉向领主申请租用镇南山坡草场，并请求将使用期限定为终身。经庄园管事查验，该片草场归领主所有，近年无人长期承租。
裁断：
莱昂子爵准许约翰·威廉取得该草场的终身使用权。约翰须依约缴纳租赋，不得擅自转租、出售或将草场另行交与他人。
此项使用权记入庄园土地簿。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: John Williams seeketh the use of the hillside meadow south of the town for the term of his life.
John Williams made suit unto the lord to rent the hillside meadow south of the town, and prayed that the term be set for his lifetime. Upon inspection by the Manor steward, it was found that the meadow belongeth to the lord, and that in recent years none had held it on any long lease.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon granteth unto John Williams the use of the said meadow for the term of his life. John must render the rents and dues according to the covenant, and may not of his own will sublet, sell, or otherwise deliver the meadow unto another.
This right of use is entered into the Manor's land book.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第248年第3案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 3, 248 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：寡妇玛莎·加西亚改嫁维克托·帕里斯后，请求登记其名下土地与财产的归属。
春日初雨后，寡妇玛莎·加西亚嫁给维克托·帕里斯，改名为玛莎·帕里斯。依其婚前名下的土地、牲畜及其他财产，均须由庄园重新登记。
裁断：
庄园确认玛莎婚前合法继承及持有的土地与财产，并准予其在婚后并入帕里斯家名下。具体田地、森林、牲畜及其他财物，由庄园书记官另行记入家产簿。
此后除非另有遗嘱或合法处分，该部分财产依帕里斯家名义管理。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: The widow Martha Garcia, having been remarried to Victor Parris, seeketh that the ownership of the land and goods held in her name be entered on record.
After the first rains of spring, the widow Martha Garcia was married to Victor Parris, and took the name Martha Parris. The land, cattle, and other goods held in her name before the marriage must all be entered anew by the Manor.
Verdict:
The Manor confirmeth the land and goods that Martha did lawfully inherit and hold before her marriage, and granteth that they be merged, after the marriage, into the name of the Parris family. The several fields, woods, cattle, and other goods shall also be entered into the book of family estate by the Manor clerk.
Hereafter, unless there be other testament or lawful disposition, this portion of goods shall be managed under the name of the Parris family.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第250年第7案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 7, 250 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：卡特·恩斯特潜入领主宅邸盗窃，并在逃离时致男仆死亡。
盛夏，莱昂子爵携家眷出游期间，卡特·恩斯特潜入领主宅邸，盗取珠宝数件。行窃时被宅邸男仆发现，卡特为逃离宅邸，与其发生争斗，致该男仆死亡。
庄园法庭将卡特·恩斯特拘押，并将此案移交治安官审理。
裁断：
经审理，卡特·恩斯特盗窃罪及杀人罪成立。治安官依律判处卡特·恩斯特绞刑。
庄园法庭将此案结果记入刑案簿。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Carter Ernst broke into the lord's dwelling to steal, and in his flight brought about the death of a manservant.
In high summer, whilst Viscount Leon was gone abroad with his household, Carter Ernst stole into the lord's dwelling and took away sundry jewels. Being spied in the act by a manservant of the house, Carter, to make his escape, fell to struggling with him, and brought about the manservant's death.
The Manor Court took Carter Ernst into custody, and delivered the case unto the Constable for hearing.
Verdict:
Upon hearing had, Carter Ernst was found guilty of theft and of manslaughter. The Constable, according to the law, sentenced Carter Ernst to be hanged.
The Manor Court entereth the outcome of this case into the roll of criminal causes.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第256年第6案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 6, 256 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：约翰·威廉以草场使用权抵押，向比利·帕特南借贷。
约翰·威廉称，其经营的土地连年歉收，无力独自维持家中生计，遂向比利·帕特南借取二十银币。双方约定，约翰·威廉以自己所租得的南坡草场作为抵押，并以放牧所得偿还借款及利息。
比利·帕特南请求庄园确认此项约定，以免日后发生争执。
裁断：
庄园准予登记此项抵押。在债务清偿之前，约翰·威廉仍可继续使用草场放牧，但不得擅自转租、出售或另行抵押。
若其未能依约偿还，比利·帕特南可依庄园法庭的裁断请求处置其相应使用权。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: John Williams, putting up his right to use the meadow as pledge, borroweth of Billy Putnam.
John Williams saith that the land he worketh hath yielded poorly year upon year, so that he is unable of himself to maintain the living of his house, and therefore borroweth twenty silver coins of Billy Putnam. It is agreed between them that John Williams putteth up the south slope meadow he holdeth on lease as pledge, and shall repay the loan and the interest thereon out of the gains of his grazing.
Billy Putnam prayeth the Manor to confirm this covenant, that no dispute may arise hereafter.
Verdict:
The Manor granteth that this pledge be entered on record. Until the debt be discharged, John Williams may yet continue to use the meadow for grazing, but may not of his own will sublet, sell, or pledge it anew.
Should he fail to repay according to the covenant, Billy Putnam may, according to the judgment of the Manor Court, seek to dispose of the said right of use.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第256年第14案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 14, 256 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：兰德·帕特南死后，比利与费思因遗产及木材归属发生争执。
盛夏，兰德·帕特南溺死于洪水中。第一场霜后，帕特南家清点其留下的田产与其他遗产。
比利·帕特南与费思·帕特南因遗产分配发生斗殴。费思称，比利偷偷砍伐了本应归自己的一片木材；比利则称，该片树林原本便未分清归属。
裁断：
在司铎乔治与母亲奥黛塔·帕特南劝说下，兄弟二人同意停止争执。双方重新清点遗产，并暂以庄园土地簿和家产记录为依据划分各自所得。
斗殴之事不再追究，此案以和解结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: After the death of Rand Putnam, Billy and Faithful fell into dispute over the inheritance and the ownership of certain timber.
In high summer, Rand Putnam drowned in the flood. After the first frost, the Putnam family took count of the fields and other goods he had left behind.
Billy Putnam and Faithful Putnam fell to blows over the dividing of the inheritance. Faithful saith that Billy had secretly felled a stand of timber that ought to have come to him; Billy saith that the ownership of that wood had never been clearly parted in the first place.
Verdict:
Upon the urging of Confessor George and of their mother, Odette Putnam, the two brothers agreed to cease their quarrel. The parties took count of the inheritance anew, and for the time being divided their several portions according to the Manor's land book and the records of family estate.
The matter of the affray is pursued no further, and this case is closed by accord.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第259年第14案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 14, 259 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：皮克托·科里请求承包领主所属磨坊。
春天，经维克托镇长担保，皮克托·科里向莱昂子爵请求接管镇上的磨坊。庄园查验后确认，皮克托此前曾修理旧水轮，并暂代磨坊事务，期间并无重大差错。
裁断：
莱昂子爵准许皮克托·科里承包磨坊。双方约定，皮克托每年须向领主上缴磨坊收入的四成，其余收入由其自行支配。
若有拖欠租赋、隐瞒收入或怠于修缮之事，领主有权收回磨坊。
此约记入庄园账簿，自当年起生效。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Pickett Corey seeketh to take on the lease of the mill belonging to the lord.
In spring, upon the surety of Magistrate Victor, Pickett Corey made suit unto Viscount Leon to take over the mill of the town. Upon inspection, the Manor confirmed that Pickett had aforetime mended the old water-wheel and had held the affairs of the mill for a season in another's stead, and that in that time there had been no great fault.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon granteth unto Pickett Corey the lease of the mill. It is agreed between them that Pickett must render up unto the lord four parts in ten of the mill's yearly income, and the rest he shall dispose of as he will.
Should there be any default in the rents and dues, any concealment of income, or any neglect of the needful repairs, the lord shall have right to take back the mill.
This covenant is entered into the Manor's account book, and taketh effect from this year forth.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第260年第33案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 33, 260 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：弗兰夫妇死于瘟疫后，其独女安妮·弗兰的遗产监护与财产处置。
向日葵花开时，丽贝卡·弗兰与其丈夫威尔·弗兰先后死于镇上的瘟疫。二人死后，仅留下女儿安妮·弗兰。
鉴于安妮尚未成年，无力独自继承并管理弗兰家的土地、牲畜及其他财产。依照弗兰夫妇生前留下的遗嘱，在安妮成年之前，弗兰家的遗产由司铎乔治与维克托镇长共同看管。
遗嘱中另有约定：弗兰家名下的土地及三头牛，全部出售给维克托镇长，价作八十银币，并附半套银餐具作为交易的一部分。
其余属于弗兰家的产业与财物，仍由司铎乔治与维克托镇长代为保管。二人不得私自变卖弗兰家的主要产业，其间所得收益须逐项记入账簿，待安妮成年后，如数交还。
另依遗嘱约定，安妮·弗兰终身拥有维克托镇长名下诊所及其院落、房屋的使用权。
裁断：
庄园法庭确认弗兰夫妇遗嘱有效。
准许司铎乔治与维克托镇长共同担任安妮·弗兰的遗产监护人与财产保管人，并依遗嘱处置弗兰家的土地、牲畜及其他财产。
弗兰家土地与三头牛归维克托镇长所有，其价作八十银币及半套银餐具。该项财产交易须记入庄园账簿。
其余遗产及代管期间所得收益，须由司铎乔治与维克托镇长妥善保管并逐项登记。待安妮成年后，应依遗嘱及账簿所记，将应归其所有的财产与收益一并交还。
安妮·弗兰对维克托镇长名下诊所、院落及房屋所享有的终身使用权，亦由庄园法庭一并登记确认。
此案记入遗产簿与土地簿。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: After the goodman Will Fran and his wife died of the plague, the guardianship of the inheritance and the disposal of the goods of their only daughter, Annie Fran.
When the sunflowers were in bloom, Rebecca Fran and her husband, Will Fran, died one after the other of the plague then in the town. After the death of the two, there remained only their daughter, Annie Fran.
Forasmuch as Annie was not yet come of age, and was unable of herself to inherit and to manage the land, cattle, and other goods of the Frans, according to the testament that the goodman Fran and his wife had left in their lifetime, the inheritance of the Frans shall, until Annie be come of age, be kept in the joint charge of Confessor George and Magistrate Victor.
It was further willed that the land held by the Frans, together with three head of cattle, be all sold unto Magistrate Victor, at the price of eighty silver coins, with half a set of silver tableware given besides as part of the bargain.
The rest of the estate and goods belonging to the Frans shall yet be kept in trust by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor. The two may not of their own accord sell off the chief estate of the Frans, and whatsoever gains arise therefrom in that time must be entered item by item into the account book, and, when Annie be come of age, rendered back to her in full.
And further, according to the will, Annie Fran shall hold, for the term of her life, the use of the apothecary that standeth in Magistrate Victor's name, together with its yard and its house.
Verdict:
The Manor Court confirmeth the will of the goodman Fran and his wife to be valid.
Confessor George and Magistrate Victor shall together serve as the guardians of the inheritance and the keepers of the goods of Annie Fran, and shall dispose of the land, cattle, and other goods of the Frans according to the testament.
The land of the Frans and three head of cattle shall belong to Magistrate Victor, at the price of eighty silver coins and half a set of silver tableware. This dealing in goods must be entered into the Manor's account book.
The rest of the inheritance, and whatsoever gains arise during the time of their trust, must be kept safe by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor and entered item by item. When Annie be come of age, the goods and gains that ought to be hers shall be rendered back to her together, according to the testament and to what is written in the account book.
The use that Annie Fran holdeth for the term of her life in the apothecary that standeth in Magistrate Victor's name, together with its yard and its house, is likewise entered and confirmed by the Manor Court.
This case is entered into the roll of inheritance and the land book.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第260年第52案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 52, 260 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：路易·沃尔控告皮克托·科里在磨坊中私藏面粉。
秋收后，路易·沃尔因怀疑磨坊私藏面粉，向庄园法庭控告磨坊管事皮克托·科里。皮克托否认私藏粮食，称磨坊中的粮食皆有账目，部分损耗乃水轮与石磨损坏所致。
裁断：
司铎乔治查阅双方账目，并询问磨坊工人与送粮农户，未能找到皮克托私藏面粉的确实证据。
在司铎乔治调解下，路易撤回控告，皮克托表示不再追究。
双方于庄园法庭前言归于好，此案结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Louis Wall accuseth Pickett Corey of hoarding flour in secret at the mill.
After the autumn harvest, Louis Wall, suspecting that flour was being hoarded in secret at the mill, brought accusation before the Manor Court against Pickett Corey, the keeper of the mill. Pickett denied the hoarding, saying that all the grain within the mill was set down in the accounts, and that some part of the loss was owing to the breaking of the water-wheel and the millstone.
Verdict:
Confessor George looked into the accounts of both parties, and questioned the mill workers and the farming folk who brought their grain, yet could find no sure proof that Pickett had hoarded flour in secret.
Upon the mediation of Confessor George, Louis withdrew his accusation, and Pickett declared that he would pursue the matter no further.
The two were reconciled before the Manor Court. This case is closed.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第262年第7案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 7, 262 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：皮克托·科里与比利·帕特南因河边空地的地界发生争执。
开春后，皮克托·科里在河边围起一片空地，并开始翻土种麦。比利·帕特南称，该处原属帕特南家旧日使用的土地，双方地界从未重新划定。
比利要求皮克托拆除围栏，归还土地。皮克托则称，此处多年无人耕种，自己承包磨坊后一直负责附近河岸，因此有权使用。
裁断：
庄园命双方暂时停止扩大耕地，不得毁坏对方已立下的界标与围栏。书记官须调取旧日土地簿与地界记录，并在必要时重新丈量。
在丈量完成之前，此案暂不作最终裁断。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Pickett Corey and Billy Putnam fell into dispute over the bounds of a plot of open ground by the river.
After the coming of spring, Pickett Corey fenced in a plot of open land by the river, and began to break the soil and sow wheat. Billy Putnam saith that the place belonged of old to land the Putnams once used, and that the bounds between the two had never been laid down anew.
Billy demanded that Pickett take down the fence and render back the land. Pickett saith that the place had lain untilled for many years, and that since taking on the lease of the mill he had kept charge of the riverbank thereabouts, and therefore had right to use it.
Verdict:
The Manor commandeth both parties for the time to cease from enlarging their tillage, and that neither destroy the boundary-marks and fences the other hath set up. The clerk must call up the old land book and the records of bounds, and, if need be, measure the ground anew.
Until the measuring be done, this case is left without final verdict for the time being.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第262年第10案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 10, 262 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：沃尔家的酒馆涉嫌替盗贼销赃，被治安官查封。
盛夏，治安官接到举报，称沃尔家的酒馆可能替过路盗贼收存并出售赃物。
治安官进入酒馆搜查，并查获数件来源不明的货物。酒馆随即被暂时查封，多特·沃尔及负责经营酒馆的人员接受问询。
裁断：
至秋收后，调查结束。治安官未能证明沃尔家明知货物来自盗贼，并主动协助销赃，也未发现沃尔家参与盗窃的证据。
因此，治安官准许解除查封，沃尔家的酒馆恢复营业。
庄园法庭记录调查结果，此案结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: The tavern of the Walls, being suspected of receiving and selling stolen goods for thieves, was shut down by the Constable.
In high summer, the Constable received report that the tavern might be keeping and selling stolen goods on behalf of thieves passing through.
The Constable entered the tavern to search, and seized sundry goods of unknown origin. The tavern was thereupon shut down for a time, and Dot Wall, together with those who had charge of the keeping of the tavern, were brought to questioning.
Verdict:
By autumn harvest, he inquiry was ended. The Constable could not prove that the Walls knew the goods to have come from thieves and had willingly helped to sell them off, nor was any proof found that the Walls partook in the theft.
Therefore the Constable granted that the seal be lifted, and the tavern of the Walls returned to its trade.
The Manor Court set down the outcome of the inquiry, and this case is closed.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第264年第7案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 7, 264 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：比利·帕特南家中的女仆搬运柴火时意外身亡，其家人请求赔偿。
深冬，比利·帕特南家中的一名女仆奉命搬运过冬所用的柴火。搬运途中，院中堆放的木柴突然倾倒，将其砸中，女仆当场身亡。
死者家人向庄园法庭陈述，该女仆年纪尚轻，平日长期承担家中杂役，早已落下腰伤。当夜，她又因打翻水盆受罚，被命不得用晚饭。
家人称，比利·帕特南及家中管事明知女仆身体有伤，又知其当日未曾进食，却仍命其独自搬运沉重木柴，亦未安排其他仆役协助。因此，死者家人请求比利·帕特南就此作出赔偿。
庄园法庭派人查验现场，确认柴垛确有倾斜，搬运时发生倒塌。比利·帕特南承认柴垛由自家仆役堆放，并称女仆当日所受惩罚与其死亡并无直接关系。
至于女仆平日劳作繁重、身有腰伤及当夜受罚之事，法庭认为皆属仆役日常事务，不足以因此归罪于主人。故庄园仅就柴垛倒塌所致死伤，以及比利·帕特南应负之责进行裁断。
裁断：
经双方协商，比利·帕特南愿向死者家人赔偿八银币。死者家人接受赔偿，并承诺此后不再就女仆之死向比利·帕特南及其家中仆役追究责任。
庄园法庭确认双方和解。
此案结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: A maidservant in the house of Billy Putnam was killed by mishap whilst carrying firewood, and her kin seek recompense.
In deep winter, a maidservant in the house of Billy Putnam was set to carry firewood for winter. As she bore it along, the woodpile stacked in the yard toppled and struck her down, and the maidservant died upon the spot.
The kin of the dead came before the Manor Court and set forth that the maidservant was yet young in years, and that having long borne the drudgery of the house, she had come by a hurt to her back some while since. That same night she had moreover been punished for overturning a basin of water, and was bidden to go without her supper.
The kin say that Billy Putnam and the steward of the house, knowing well that the maidservant was hurt in body, and knowing too that she had not eaten that day, did nonetheless bid her carry the heavy wood alone, and set no other servant to help her. Therefore the kin of the dead seek that Billy Putnam make recompense.
The Manor Court sent men to view the place, and confirmed that the woodpile did indeed lean awry, and had toppled in the course of the carrying. Billy Putnam owned that the woodpile had been stacked by his own servants, but said that the punishment the maidservant had suffered that day bore no direct part in her death.
As for the maidservant's heavy daily labor, her back injury, and the punishment she suffered that night, the Court holdeth these to be the common lot of servants, not enough to lay blame upon the master. Therefore the Manor giveth judgment only touching the death caused by the toppling woodpile, and the responsibility Billy Putnam ought to bear therein.
Verdict:
Upon agreement between the parties, Billy Putnam is willing to pay the kin of the dead eight silver coins. The kin accept, and promise that hereafter they will not call Billy Putnam or his servants to answer again for the maidservant's death.
The Manor Court confirmeth the accord.
The case is closed.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第265年第10案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 10, 265 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：吉尔斯·沃伦拖欠酒债，酒馆请求庄园追讨。
吉尔斯·沃伦长期在酒馆赊取酒水，欠下酒债后多次未能偿还。酒馆主人遂向庄园法庭请求追讨。
经查，吉尔斯确有酒债未清，且无力立即支付。
裁断：
庄园命吉尔斯·沃伦限期清偿债务。因其无力以现银偿还，准其变卖部分牲畜，以所得钱款抵偿酒债。
债务结清后，吉尔斯获释。
庄园法庭告诫其日后不得再以无力偿还之财物赊取酒水。
此案结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Giles Warren oweth a drink-debt unpaid, and the tavern seeketh to have the Manor recover it.
Giles Warren had long taken drink upon credit at the tavern, and having run up a debt, failed many times over to repay it. The keeper of the tavern thereupon prayed the Manor Court to recover the same.
Upon examination, it was found that Giles did indeed have a debt unpaid, and that he was unable to pay it out of hand.
Verdict:
The Manor commandeth Giles Warren to clear the debt within a set term. Forasmuch as he was unable to repay in ready silver, it is granted that he sell off some part of his cattle, and with the money so gotten make satisfaction of the debt.
The debt being cleared, Giles is set free.
The Manor Court giveth him warning that hereafter he shall not take drink upon credit against goods he is unable to pay.
The case is closed.

Title.SourceString: 《圣阿尔博镇庄园法庭记录》建镇后的第266年第1案
Title.LocalizedString: St. Arbor Manor Court Rolls — Case 1, 266 Years Since the Town's Founding

Page.SourceString:
案由：安妮·弗兰成年后，请求取回由司铎乔治与维克托镇长代为看管的遗产。
新年后，安妮·弗兰成年，依照父母遗嘱向庄园法庭请求取回弗兰夫妇留下的遗产。司铎乔治与维克托镇长提交了多年间的财产账簿，供庄园查验。
裁断：
经核查，庄园确认安妮已具备独立继承与管理家产的资格。
司铎乔治与维克托镇长须将弗兰夫妇留下的遗产及相关账簿一并交还安妮·弗兰。作为感谢，安妮许诺在未来三年内免费为维克托镇长家提供草药。
自此以后，弗兰家的财产由安妮自行继承与管理，此案结案。
Page.LocalizedString:
Cause of Action: Annie Fran, being come of age, prayeth to take back the inheritance kept in trust by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor.
After the New Year, Annie Fran came of age, and according to her parents' will sought to have the Manor Court restore the inheritance the goodman Fran and his wife left behind. Confessor George and Magistrate Victor rendered up the account books of the several years, for the Manor to examine.
Verdict:
Upon examination, the Manor confirmeth that Annie is now fit to inherit and to manage the family's goods in her own right.
Confessor George and Magistrate Victor must render back to Annie Fran the inheritance the goodman Fran and his wife had left, together with the account books thereto belonging. In token of her thanks, Annie promiseth to furnish herbs to Magistrate Victor's household free of charge for the next three years.
From this time forth, the goods of the Fran family are Annie's own to inherit and to manage. The case is closed.

Page.SourceString:
建镇后的第262年，春耕时，为卢娜之子特里克购买施威夏特的橡树林和十条田，十八银币。邮递及文书钱，五铜币。另，从弗兰家遗产中暂支十八银币，秋收后补还。
建镇后的第264年，化雪时，卖谷地北边的白桦林给比利，获二十二银币；钱已收，地契已改。
建镇后的第265年，新年前，把玛莎带来的老井旁的二十条田卖给比利，获十五银币；钱已收，地契已改。
建镇后的第265年，新年前，向多特求购半套磨掉姓名的银餐具，十银币；
建镇后的第266年，新年后，将弗兰家的遗产归还安妮，共计八十五银币和半套银餐具；账目已平。
Page.LocalizedString:
In the 262nd year after the town was founded, during the spring plowing, purchased Shweishate's oak woods and ten fields for Luna's son Derrick, eighteen silver coins. The postage and clerical fee was five copper coins. Additionally, they advanced eighteen silver coins from the Fran family's estate, to be repaid after the autumn harvest.
In the 264th year after the town was founded, during the thaw, they sold the birch woods north of the valley to Billy for twenty-two silver coins. The payment was received, and the deed was amended.
In the 265th year after the town was founded, before New Year's, they sold Billy the twenty fields beside the old well that Martha had brought into the family, for fifteen silver coins. The payment was received, and the deed was amended.
In the 265th year after the town was founded, before New Year's, purchased half a set of silver tableware with the names filed off from Dot for ten silver coins;
In the 266th year after the town was founded, after New Year's, returned the Fran family's estate to Annie, totaling eighty-five silver coins and half a set of silver tableware; all accounts settled.

Page.SourceString:
亲爱的维克托：
好久不见，你在家乡过得还好吗？我想请莱昂子爵给特里克一份工作，可他怎么也不肯。我问过现在还在庄园里帮佣的莱斯特，莱昂老爷似乎也有些自顾不暇了。虽然他们一家表面上还维持着贵族的气派，可从瘟疫那年开始，便大不如前了。
想想也是，那时死了太多人，加上战争，好多土地都荒了，他每年收上来的地租少了快一半。
听说你现在的生活好极了，我真是为你高兴，若是你能帮特里克找份工作就更好了，我想让他去见见你，你说好吗？有些话，也许还是该由一个做父亲的人来说。我只希望这孩子能打起精神，好好生活，别再沉迷于赌桌和酒杯。
爱你的，
卢娜·科波特
Page.LocalizedString:
Dear Victor,
It's been long since we met, and I trust you fare well in our old home. I sought to have the Viscount Leon give Derrick a place, yet by no means would he agree to it. I asked of Lester, who serves still in the Manor, and it seems the good Lord Leon is hard pressed enough in his own affairs. Though the family keep up the airs of the nobility for all to see, they have been much diminished since the year of the plague.
And no wonder, for so many died in that time, and with the war besides, much of the land lies fallow, and the rents he gathers each year are fallen near by half.
I hear your life is now most prosperous, and I do rejoice for you with all my heart. Should you be able to find Derrick some work, that would be better still. If you are willing, I would have him come and see you. Some things, perhaps, are best said by one who is himself a father. I ask only that the boy might take heart and live rightly, and give himself no more to the gaming table and the cup.
Love,
Luna Cobblepot

此后，维克托·帕里斯及其家人不得再以旧界、旧约或其他理由主张该地。

Page.SourceString:
第九轮圆月夜
来自海外的香料，四罐，杰克大副供，卖八十银币；
吉尔斯欠筹码十二枚；
吉尔斯欠三杯朗姆酒；
两匹紫色丝绸，外层有勾丝，刀疤脸汉克斯供，卖三十二银币；
费思从城中拿回来的一只金牙，换筹码十枚；
刀疤脸汉克斯提供邻国士兵的劫掠路线，卖三银币；
今夜酒水收入六银币又八枚铜币，筹码收入八银币与一只金牙；
下一轮圆月夜，需支付杰克大副七十五银币，刀疤脸汉克斯二十四银币；附近巡查治安官二银币；

从前，有一个国王。他统治着一片辽阔而丰饶的土地。
那里曾有金色的麦田，山坡上长满青草，河水从不冻结。春天来得很早，秋天也总是很晚。人们说，那是因为神明一直注视着这片土地。
国王年轻时英勇善战。他带领军队赢得了一场又一场战争，土地越来越辽阔，城堡越来越高，向他俯首的人也越来越多。
于是，国王渐渐相信，这一切都是凭借自己的力量得来的。
后来，他不再仰望天空。他忘记了是谁让种子发芽，让河流解冻，让牲畜平安度过冬天。
神明因此收回了自己的目光。
而一直躲藏在阴影里的恶魔，终于伸出了手。
Page.LocalizedString:
Once, there was a king. He ruled over a vast and fertile land.
There were golden wheat fields, hills lush with green, and rivers that never froze. Spring came early, and autumn always arrived late. People said it was due to the Highest One's continued vigilance over the land.
When the king was young, he was brave and victorious in battle. He led his armies to win one war after another. His lands spread farther, his castles grew taller, and more and more people bowed before him.
And so, the king gradually came to believe that all of this had been achieved through his own strength.
In time, he no longer looked upwards. He forgot who made the seeds sprout, the rivers thaw, and the livestock survive the winter in peace.
The Highest One therefore withdrew Its gaze.
And the Devil, who had been hiding among the shadows all the while, finally reached out its hand.

Page.SourceString:
第一年，冬天来得比往常更早。
第二年，春天迟迟没有到来。
河水封冻，牧草枯死，小麦还没有成熟，便被霜雪压倒在地。人们开始挨饿。
他们杀掉牲畜，吃掉储藏的粮食，又开始吃本该留到明年的种子。
可是冬天并没有结束。
冰雪一年比一年厚，夏天一年比一年短。有些村庄在暴雪中失去了道路，有些孩子还没有长大，便在寒冷和饥饿中死去。
人们害怕极了。他们说，是恶魔来到了这里。
恶魔藏在长夜里，藏在饥饿里，也藏在人们的心中。它让人忘记祈祷，让人怀疑神明，让人不再相信彼此。
于是，恶魔的党羽渐渐多了起来。他们混在人群之中，说冬天永远不会结束。他们说，神明已经抛弃了所有人。他们还说，只要向恶魔低头，就能换来粮食、温暖和活下去的机会。
终于，在又一个漫长的冬天里，国王低下了骄傲的头颅。
Page.LocalizedString:
In the first year, winter came earlier than usual.
In the second year, spring was late.
The rivers froze, the pasture withered, and the wheat was beaten to the ground by frost and snow before it had ripened. The people began to starve.
They slaughtered their livestock, ate their stored grain, and then began eating the seeds meant to be saved for the following year.
But winter did not end.
The ice and snow grew thicker each year, while summer grew shorter. Some villages lost their roads beneath the blizzards. Some children died from cold and hunger before they even reached adulthood.
The people were terrified. They said the Devil had finally come.
The Devil hid in the long nights, in the hunger, and in people's hearts. It made them forget how to pray, doubt the Highest One, and lose faith in one another.
And so, the Devil's followers gradually grew in number. They mingled among the people, saying that winter would never end. They said the Highest One had abandoned them all. They also said that if people bowed their heads to the Devil, they could trade their submission for food, warmth, and a chance to survive.
At last, during yet another endless winter, the king lowered his proud head.

Page.SourceString:
国王跪在空荡荡的教堂中，请求神明重新注视他的土地。
可是神明告诉他：“我从未离开。是你们在漫长的寒冬里，渐渐忘记了该往哪里走。”
国王问：“那么，我们该怎样驱逐恶魔？”
神明回答：“先让自己的心重新拥有光。”
于是，国王命人重新敲响钟声。人们回到教堂，重新祈祷，重新帮助那些失去粮食和家园的人。
他们不再轻信黑暗中的低语，也不再追随那些许诺捷径的人。因为他们终于明白：
恶魔最喜欢寒冷。而比寒冷更可怕的，是一颗已经习惯了寒冷的心。
所以，孩子啊。要做一个虔诚而忠实的人。
不要被黑暗中的声音迷惑，不要相信那些教你背弃信仰的人。只要人们仍然相信光明，并坚定地向着它走去——
再漫长的冬天，也终有结束的一天。
Page.LocalizedString:
The king knelt in the empty church, begging the Highest One to look upon his land once more.
But the Highest One told him, "I never left. It was you who gradually forgot where to go during the endless winter."
The king asked, "Then how can we drive out the Devil?"
The Highest One replied, "First, let the light return to your hearts."
So the king ordered the bells to ring once more. The people returned to the church, prayed again, and helped those who had lost their provisions and homes.
They no longer trusted the whispers in the darkness, nor followed those who promised them shortcuts. At last, they understood:
The Devil loves the cold above all. But, more frightening than the cold, is a heart that has grown accustomed to it.
So, child… be devout and faithful.
Do not be deceived by the voices in the darkness and do not believe those who would teach you to abandon your faith. So long as people still believe in the light and steadfastly walk toward it—
even an endless winter will one day come to an end.

Page.SourceString:
亲爱的日记：
我爸爸总是指责比利先生品德不够高尚，认为我应该嫁给庄园里的管家或是男佣，可他根本不知道，这些话在我看来是多么虚伪！
他以为我不知道呢！他藏在桌子抽屉里面的那封信！他从前在庄园里，有一个情人，而我有一个同父异母的哥哥！
我讨厌他，可是我又不能报复他，我可怜的妈妈身体不好，经不起这样的打击！
比利先生家正缺个女仆，或许我可以过去，毕竟以我的身份，他不至于对我太差，只会让我干些轻松的活。而且他英俊帅气，善于经营，虽然他现在被安妮迷住了，但这是一时的，就像我爸爸那样。如果我们能够结婚，我一定不会让他变成我爸爸那种人！
最重要的是，我也不用总是面对着爸爸妈妈，仿佛被夹在中间似的。等我想好了该怎么办，我再回来就行了，他们肯定不舍得真的打我！就这样决定了，拿了爸爸私藏的银币，明天就走。或许应该先进城一趟，我还没进过城呢，去看看再回来吧！尤其是听说城里每天都在吊死人，一定有趣极了！
等我拿了银币，他会不会知道，我看过那封信了？不过这样也好，他肯定不敢当着妈妈的面指责我，或许还能对妈妈再好一点！
Page.LocalizedString:
Dear Diary:
Father is always criticizing Mr. Billy for not being virtuous enough, saying I should marry the manor's butler or one of the male servants. But he has no idea how hypocritical that sounds to me!
He thinks I don't know about that letter he hid in the table drawer! He used to have a lover at the manor, and I have an older half-brother from that affair!
I hate him, but I can't take revenge on him. Mother is in poor health and couldn't withstand such a shock!
Mr. Billy's household is looking for a maid. Maybe I could go there. Given my status, he wouldn't treat me too badly—he'd only give me easy work. Besides, he's handsome, charming, and good with money. He's infatuated with Annie right now, but that's only temporary, just like my father. If we got married, I'd never let him become the kind of man my father is!
Most importantly, I wouldn't have to keep facing my father and mother. Once I've figured out what to do, I can come back. They wouldn't really have the heart to hit me! It's decided, then. I'll take Father's hidden stash of silver coins and leave at first light tomorrow. Maybe I should go into the city first. I've never been there, so I'll take a look and come back! Especially since I've heard they hang people there every day. It must be exciting!
Once I take the silver coins, will he realize that I've read the letter? Perhaps that's for the best. He certainly wouldn't dare criticize me in front of Mother. Maybe he'd even treat her a little better!

HeiYu_FenWei_Interact_46.Comment: 黑羽主线-后日谈异管局档案

Page.SourceString:
……
以上是我搜集的近两百年来「猎巫」异象案例汇总，自鉴定师零处问询来的「猎巫」异象（即歧骸「审判官」）泯除过程，同时附上了「审判官」诞生的时代背景以及「魔女审判」的更多历史细节。
仔细分析这些案例的来龙去脉，不难看出，「猎巫」异象作为一种迷因异象，和集体意志的变化存在紧密的关联。这或许可以解决本次异象泯除过程中，一个最大的疑惑——为什么歧骸「审判官」会在此时出现在海特洛。梅露菈自称，是因为自己的力量在减弱，无法继续困住「审判官」。但我认为，这只是她因为不了解异能造物，误解了自己的能力。
首先，梅露菈和其他圣阿尔博镇镇民一样，是那个时代的虔诚宗教徒。虽然她深知魔女审判残暴而荒谬，但从未因此放弃自身的信仰。在她看来，「血肉之笼」不是她的异能造物，而是她做为魔女，从恶魔处交易来的某种诅咒或法术。她并不知道，异能者需要刻苦练习来掌握和提升自己的异能，因此她从未尝试掌控自己造出的「血肉之笼」，甚至完全不认为自己是它的主人；否则，她或许早就能离开「血肉之笼」，免于几百年的灼烧之苦。
她与「审判官」一起被困在「血肉之笼」中几百年，直到近年，随着海特洛的城市开发扩大，星沉湾的人流量渐长，民宿、酒店等为商旅游客提供的服务设施也逐渐增加。歧骸「审判官」做为一种迷因异象，在这个过程中，借助外界密集的人类活动，不断从人们心中摄取滋长痛苦以滋长自身力量。因此，并非是梅露菈的力量在消退，而是歧骸「审判官」的力量在缓慢积累，直到足以突破「血肉之笼」。
一般来说，这份报告到此即可结束，但为了帮助管理局的后辈们更好地处理「猎巫」异象，我想附上一些自己浅薄的思考。
在鉴定师经历的这场「魔女审判」中，我看到当时的人们，面对着难以解决的自然灾害、瘟疫和无法控制的社会变动，内心产生了极大的痛苦。最终，他们为了解决这些痛苦，选择相信审判官的话——只要消灭魔女，就可以解决一切问题。于是，人们寻找各种理由，指控和伤害自己讨厌的人、身边的弱者、还有自身利益的竞争者。更加不幸的是，在当时的时代背景下，女性最是首当其冲。
虽然，因为时代的变化和「魔女审判」的消失，「审判官」失去了支撑它的恶意，最终自然泯除，但是，「猎巫」异象从未从我们的历史中消失，相反，它总是如影子般甩不开……
事实上，只要将魔女换一个名字，譬如——异能者，那么便能诞生一个崭新的「猎巫」异象。
根据管理局/白蜡树记载，40年余年前，异常大规模爆发后的五年内，仅仅是记录在案的「猎巫」异象就有八起，其中有两起均为IV级异象。当时的调查报告显示，八起「猎巫」异象皆源于当时人类对异象和异能者的恐惧。在多个规模不一的城市中，都诞生了相似的以剿灭异能者为宗旨的群体，当时的「猎巫」异象便是这样诞生的。那时的异能者，和鉴定师遇到的魔女一样，在普通人眼中，是一切灾难的源头，是人们恐惧的对象，自然也是所有罪名的承担者。
若是继续向前追溯历史，我们除了审判过魔女和异能者外，还发明过许多特别的词汇用来定义被排斥的异己。仿佛只要能够用这种特别的词汇称呼异己，就能够合理地将他们开除出人类，使他们沦为某种牲畜都不如的东西。同时，人们也坚信，只要消灭他们，自己当下的全部痛苦都将随之消失，所以无论用何种方式消灭他们，都是合情合理甚至合法的。
可实际上，人们只是在消灭异己的过程中，暂时遗忘了当下的痛苦。这样消灭异己的行动，从未真正解决过任何痛苦，也不可能解决任何痛苦。
既然如此，我们为什么依然乐此不疲的重复着相似的行为呢？即便在现代社会，在文明的约束下，像「魔女审判」那样合法且光明正大的屠杀并不常见，也很难诞生高级别的「猎巫」异象，但类似的事情依然以更为隐秘的形式出现在我们周边。
这是我第一次深入研读这么多「猎巫」异象的调查报告。就在我为这种集体的悲剧的重复发生感到无力与困惑时，我在其中一个较为古老的报告中，发现了一位前辈留下的随笔，他的话令我稍感欣慰，或许我们有办法终结这样的事，只是需要很长的很长的时间。因为前辈的字迹已经模糊不清，很可能被后辈们在研读时忽略，所以我想引用在这里，方便后辈们阅读，并以此作结：
「邪恶并不总来自决心作恶的人，也可能来自停止思考、只执行职责的人。他们并非不知道善恶，而是不再愿意承担判断善恶的责任。他们把自己的选择交给命令、规则和群体，于是最终连自己为何而行动都不再知晓。这令人叹息，但也令人欣慰。因为这至少证明，人并非只能服从。只要有人愿意重新承担判断的责任，愿意在行动之前问自己“我正在做什么”，那么这样的异象便不会轻易诞生。」
该写的，狗狗人都写完了，本来可以给局里省下一张纸的，但是看到他最后的狗屁感想，我不得不浪费纸张了。（措辞需修改）（不改）
狗狗喜欢人类，他才会有那种天真的幻想。他还是没想明白，思考不是获得答案的道路，而是承受没有答案的开始。思考迫使一个人自己判断，自己选择，自己承担错误，自己面对未知。没有人告诉他答案，也没有人为他承担后果。这就是自由，大多数人承担不起的自由。
人类渴望自由，却也渴望有人替自己承担自由带来的痛苦，可不是人人都像我这样能享受痛苦的恩赐。那些庸人为了免于痛苦，愿意付出任何代价。只要你能给他们一个答案，答案是不是真相根本不重要，重要的是，答案是确定的。所以他们就是喜欢一个审判官来到他们面前，告诉他们，相信我，杀了魔女就万事大吉，然后他们就相信审判官放的任何狗屁。
我以为我们处理过那两次小型「猎巫」异象后，他早就明白了呢……对鉴定师看到的时代来说，他们需要的不是神明，而是奇迹！对于现在的人来说，他们需要的不是思考的自由，而是确定的答案！
尤其是在饥饿、瘟疫和战争面前，大多数人根本没有余裕思考。狗狗自以为让人们学会思考就万事大吉，却忘了这背后的自由也是一种奢侈，不是人人都承担得起的。所以，人们渴望一名审判官。
报告人：
E.T.D四队翳
E.T.D四队法帝娅
Page.LocalizedString:
……
The above is a summary I have compiled of witch-hunting anomaly cases from the past two hundred years, together with the nullification process for the witch-hunting anomaly (that is, the oddity known as the "Inquisitor") as learned through the report from Appraiser Zero. I have also appended the historical background in which the Inquisitor came into being, along with further historical detail on the witch trials.
Having analyzed the full course of these cases closely, I found it easy to associate the memetic witch-hunting anomaly with shifts in the collective will. This could explain the single greatest puzzle in its nullification process: why the oddity known as the Inquisitor appeared in Hethereau at this time. Merula claimed it was because her powers weakened, such that she could no longer keep the Inquisitor contained. But I believe she misunderstood her own powers, out of a lack of understanding of esper constructs.
First, Merula, like the other townsfolk of St. Arbor, was a devout believer in the faith of that era. Though she knew well the cruelty and absurdity of the witch trials, she never gave up her faith on that account. As she saw it, the Fleshbound Cage was not her esper construct, but rather some magical curse that she, as a witch, had bargained from the Devil. She did not know that an esper must train hard to master and strengthen their ability, and so she never once tried to take control of the Fleshbound Cage she created. In fact, she did not think of herself as its master at all. Otherwise, she might long since have left the Fleshbound Cage, and been spared her hundreds of years of burning torment.
She and the Inquisitor were trapped in the Fleshbound Cage for hundreds of years. Then, in recent years, Hethereau developed. Foot traffic through Starfall Bay grew, and guesthouses, hotels, and other services for travelers multiplied. Through all this, the memetic Inquisitor fed ceaselessly on the pain it drew from the people around it, growing its own power. So it was not that Merula's power was fading, but that the Inquisitor's was slowly building, until at last it could break free of the Fleshbound Cage.
Normally, this report would have ended here. But to help the Bureau's younger members better handle witch-hunting anomalies, I would like to append a few humble thoughts of my own.
In the witch trial the Appraiser experienced, I saw people in tremendous pain. They faced natural disasters they could not resolve, including plague and social upheaval beyond their control. To ease that pain, they chose to believe the Inquisitor: destroy the witches, and every problem would be solved. They cast about for any reason to accuse and harm the people they disliked: the weak and their rivals. Worse still, given the times, it was women who bore the brunt of it.
Though the changing of the times and the dwindling of the witch trials stripped the Inquisitor of the malice that sustained it, and it was at last nullified of its own accord, witch-hunting anomalies have never disappeared from our history. On the contrary, they have always haunted us like a specter we cannot shake…
As a matter of fact, change "witches" to something else, like "espers," then you get fertile ground for a new witch-hunting anomaly.
According to records from the Bureau and Fraxinus, five years after the great outbreak over forty years ago, there were eight witch-hunting anomalies on record, two of them Class IV. Investigation reports showed all eight arose from humanity's fear of anomalies and espers. In cities large and small, similar groups sprang up, each bent on wiping out espers, and so the era's witch-hunting anomalies were born. The espers of that time, like the witches the Appraiser encountered, were in ordinary eyes the source of every disaster, the object of fear, and so, naturally, the ones made to bear every accusation.
If we trace history back further, we'll find that beyond putting witches and espers on trial, we have coined many special words to define those we cast out. As though a single such word could rightfully expel them from the human race and reduce them to something lower than any beast. People believed, too, that once the outcasts were dealt with, all their own pain would vanish with them, so dealing with them by any means was reasonable, righteous, and even lawful.
But in truth, purging the outcasts only made people briefly forget their present pain. Such actions never truly resolved any of that pain, nor ever could.
If that's the case, why do we repeat such behavior again and again? In modern society, under present-day constraints, lawful and brazen killings as seen in witch trials are now uncommon, and high-level witch-hunting anomalies rarely arise. Nevertheless, similar things happen all around us, just in more subdued forms.
This was my first time studying so many witch-hunting anomaly reports in depth. Just as I sat helpless and bewildered at the repetition of these collective tragedies, I found a note in one of the older reports, left by a predecessor. His words gave me a small measure of comfort. Perhaps there is a way to end such things. It will only take a very, very long time. The predecessor's handwriting has grown faint, and those who study the reports after us will likely pass it over. So I want to quote it here, for them to read more easily, and to close with it:
"Evil does not always originate from those set on doing wrong. It can also come from those who cease thinking and merely follow orders. It is not that they cannot tell good from evil, but that they no longer care to bear the responsibility of making up their own minds. They surrender their choices to orders, to rules, and to the mob, until in the end they no longer know what they are doing. This is cause for sorrow, but also for comfort. For it proves, at least, that people are not bound only to obey. As long as people take up their responsibilities, and ask what they are doing before they act, witch-hunting anomalies will not easily come to be."
Alright, I originally thought Doggo pretty much said what's left to say and I meant to save the Bureau some paper, but after reading his BS conclusion, I had to throw in my two cents. (Mind your language) (Nah)
Doggo likes humans, that's the only reason he clings to that naive little fantasy. He still hasn't figured it out: contemplation is not a journey to answers, but the beginning of the acceptance of the lack thereof. Contemplation forces you to judge, choose, and own the mistakes you make, such that you face the unknown all by yourself. Nobody can give you answers, and nobody can bear the consequences of your own actions. That's freedom for you, and most people find the burden too heavy.
Humans crave freedom, yet they also crave someone to shoulder the pain that comes with freedom. Not everyone can savor pain the way I do. Those riffraff would pay any price to spare themselves such pain. Give them an answer and it doesn't matter in the slightest whether it's true, as long as they consider it beyond doubt. That's why they love it when an Inquisitor shows up and tells them: Trust me, kill the witches and everything will be fine. And that's how they'll eat up any nonsense the Inquisitor spoonfeeds them.
And here I thought he'd have figured it out ages ago, after we handled those two little witch-hunting anomalies together… For the era the Appraiser witnessed, what those people needed wasn't a deity but a miracle! As for people today, what they need isn't the freedom to think but a definitive answer!
Especially in the face of hunger, plague, and war, most people have no room to think at all. Doggo assumes that teaching people to think will set everything right, but he forgets that the freedom that enables thinking is something of a luxury—not everyone can afford its cost. And thus, people long for Inquisitors.
Submitted by:
Skia, ETD-4
Fadia, ETD-4
